subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: Should Telegram channel_post commands ignore sender-scoped groups[chatId].allowFrom and authorize only by explicit chat allow, or should configured sender-scoped allowFrom make channel_post commands unsupported or fail closed?
rationale: This is an authorization boundary on a Telegram surface without a normal human sender, and current code/docs support both plausible interpretations without declaring the intended security contract.

options.title: Fail Closed When Sender Scope Is Configured
options.body: Treat sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom as unsupported for channel_post commands, return a clear message, and document that channel posts cannot prove a human sender.

options.title: Use Explicit Chat Allow Only
options.body: Allow channel_post commands from explicitly configured channel chats and document that sender-scoped allowFrom is intentionally ignored on that surface.

options.title: Defer To Broader Bot-To-Bot Design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work defines channel sender identity, peer-bot intake, and loop controls together.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed When Sender Scope Is Configured
recommendation.body: Treat sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom as unsupported for channel_post commands, return a clear message, and document that channel posts cannot prove a human sender.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the security/defaults and channel authorization boundary where history points to this person as an adjacent policy and docs contributor.
